title: Output limit bypass via tag balancer appending unclosed language tags
causal_explanation: OutputSink enforces the 128 KiB limit during parsing events. However, balance_language_tags runs after parsing on sink.buffer and appends closing tags (e.g. </ru>) without size checks. An input with 14,564 unclosed <ru> tags produces 131,077 bytes, exceeding MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES (128 KiB).
impact: POST /prepare can return responses larger than MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.
remedy: Add an explicit length check in balance_language_tags or check final string length against max_output_bytes before returning Ok.

title: Queue-dropped prepare job leaves ghost entry in inFlightPrepares
causal_explanation: In schedulePrepareJob, when prepareQueue exceeds 8 items, the oldest waiter is rejected via dropped.reject. In the dropped job's IIFE, the rejection occurs at the queue wait `await new Promise(...)` (line 409) which is outside the `try { ... } finally { ... }` block (line 416). Consequently, inFlightPrepares.delete(key) is never called for the dropped job, leaving a permanently rejected Promise in the map.
impact: Subsequent calls to schedulePrepareJob for the exact same message/revision return the cached rejected Promise via the deduplication check.
remedy: Wrap the queue-wait await inside the try block or add a catch handler to delete the inFlightPrepares entry if the queue rejects.

title: Foreground synthesis rejects its own result from cache when discovering new server revision
causal_explanation: In synthesize(), currentGeneration is captured before await synthesizeConfigured(). If the response carries a new synthesisRevision, line 376 calls cache.invalidateRevision() which increments this.generation. Line 380 then passes the stale currentGeneration to cache.set(), which rejects it because jobGeneration < this.generation.
impact: Audio is returned to caller, but not cached on the first request discovering a new revision, forcing a redundant fetch on the next play.
remedy: Re-capture this.cache.generation after calling invalidateRevision before passing it to cache.set().

title: Zombie foreground lease when tab disconnects without calling releaseForeground
causal_explanation: acquireForeground sets `until: Date.now() + 15_000`, but isForegroundActive() checks only `this.activeLeases.size > 0` without evaluating lease.until. If a browser tab crashes or abruptly closes, the lease remains in the map until process restart.
impact: Speculative background synthesis remains suspended because isForegroundActive() permanently returns true.
remedy: In isForegroundActive(), lazily purge leases where Date.now() > lease.until before checking size.

title: Punctuation break divergence between client.js and speech-text.js on semicolons and newlines
causal_explanation: In speech-text.js line 186, nextSpeechCut looks for semicolon (`; `) and newline (`\n`). In client.js line 216, the embedded copy of nextSpeechCut omits `; ` and `\n`. On text containing semicolons, the client creates different chunk cuts than coordinator.messageFirstChunk(), causing speculative cache misses.
impact: Cache misses for speculative chunk 0 on messages containing semicolons.
remedy: Synchronize the punctuation list in client.js nextSpeechCut to include `; ` and `\n`.

title: Volume slider not mounted in rendered player card DOM
causal_explanation: setPlaybackVolume and playback.volume (0..1) exist in client.js, but the JSX/createElement tree in TeraTtsAction renders only play button, progress range slider, -10s, rate, +15s, and stop buttons. The volume input element was not added to the sub-row.
impact: Volume is set to 1.0 by default, but no UI control is rendered to adjust it.
remedy: Add an input[type=range] volume control to the player card sub-row or header.

title: Unconditional claim of latency-neutrality for spinning=0 and missing cgroup error check
causal_explanation: README claims spinning=0 reduces CPU time 'without degrading latency'. On a lightly-loaded machine with a single serial client, wake-up latency may be masked. In tools/bench_profile.py, if the cgroup path is missing, read_cgroup_stats defaults to 0, which would report 0 throttled periods even if cgroup was unmonitored.
impact: Documentation claim is broader than measured scope; benchmark tool should fail fast if cgroup file cannot be read.
remedy: Clarify in README that spinning=0 benefits cgroup quota under concurrent loads; assert cgroup file presence in benchmark script.
